comments.body:
Preflight progress (2026-08-15, worktree ../release-0.12.0 at origin/main 95f97cbeb6):
- Versions bumped in lockstep: pyproject.toml 0.12.0, server.json top-level + packages[].version 0.12.0, uv.lock root package 0.12.0 (uv lock && uv lock --check exit 0). release_guards.py version-lockstep exits 0.
- CHANGELOG: found a pre-existing defect — TWO '## [Unreleased]' headers (lines 11 and 102; the second introduced when the pre-1.0 pass #3 removals were prepended without merging). Merged both into one hand-curated '## [0.12.0] - 2026-08-15' section (four BREAKING pre-1.0 removals folded into the Removed subsection), fresh empty [Unreleased] above, footer compare links updated ([unreleased]: v0.12.0...HEAD, [0.12.0]: v0.11.0...v0.12.0).
- Green: tests/unit/test_release_guards.py + test_release_workflow_pins.py (40 passed), make lint, make typecheck, python -m build (nava_rebar-0.12.0 wheel+sdist), twine check PASSED (via uvx; twine is not in the dev venv — it is CI release-lock-pinned only).
- make test first run: 47 failed/41 errors, ALL in git-on-temp-bare-repo fixtures. Root-caused as environmental: the agent harness shell injects GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit via env, so git refuses the cwd-discovered bare origin.git dirs the fixtures create ('fatal: not in a git directory'). Reproduces identically on the untouched main checkout at the already-CI-green landed commit; with the injected keys removed (env -u GIT_CONFIG_*) all 88 previously-failed tests pass. Not repository evidence; full clean make test re-run in progress.

## Context
Cut the next minor release, 0.12.0, from reviewed main using docs/releasing.md. The current package and latest tag are 0.11.0/v0.11.0. PyPI is immutable; publication must use the dispatch-from-main workflow and its required pypi environment approval. The release date is 2026-08-15. Closed ticket reflective-sticky-grouper (9874-b1a9-2ff1-4cd3) is the 0.11.0 release precedent, not active duplicate work. CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] section already holds hand-curated entries, so per docs/releasing.md step 1a the changelog step is a retitle of [Unreleased] to [0.12.0] - 2026-08-15 (fresh empty [Unreleased] above it, compare links updated), not a make changelog regeneration.

## Plan
- Work in a fresh worktree based on current origin/main and confirm release prerequisites, identity, recent Gerrit history/rights, and channel state.
- Bump pyproject.toml and every version in server.json to 0.12.0; regenerate uv.lock so the root project version remains locked at 0.12.0; retitle CHANGELOG.md's curated [Unreleased] section to [0.12.0] - 2026-08-15 with a fresh empty [Unreleased] and correct compare links.
- Run version-lockstep and proportional release preflight: release-specific tests/guards, lock-currentness, lint, typecheck, full tests, build, and twine checks.
- Commit with DCO, Change-Id, and rebar-ticket trailer; send through Gerrit and wait for LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with no unresolved comments, then Submit.
- After the bump lands on main, dispatch release.yml from main with version=0.12.0 and obtain the required pypi environment approval; monitor the entire workflow to a terminal result.
- Verify PyPI 0.12.0 plus PEP 740 provenance, the v0.12.0 GitHub tag/release and artifacts, MCP Registry 0.12.0, and the Homebrew tap bump (trigger autobump if useful).
- Install nava-rebar[mcp]==0.12.0 from PyPI in the distribution-channel environment and run the packaged post-publication probe.
- Record receipts and results on this ticket, then close it only after all acceptance criteria are met.

## File impact
- pyproject.toml — package version bump
- server.json — MCP manifest/package version bump
- uv.lock — root package version lockstep with pyproject.toml
- CHANGELOG.md — retitled curated 0.12.0 release section and compare links

## Rollback / failure policy
Before publish, stop on any failed guard, review, or CI vote and remediate through a new Gerrit patchset. After publish, PyPI cannot be replaced: if the artifact is bad, yank 0.12.0, de-list its GitHub Release, and cut a fixed patch version; do not overwrite artifacts or retag published content.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] pyproject.toml declares version 0.12.0.
- [ ] server.json top-level version is 0.12.0.
- [ ] Every server.json packages[].version is 0.12.0.
- [ ] uv.lock records the root nava-rebar package at version 0.12.0 and `uv lock --check` exits 0.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md contains a hand-curated 0.12.0 section dated 2026-08-15.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md has a fresh Unreleased section and correct 0.12.0 compare links.
- [ ] `python scripts/release_guards.py version-lockstep --version 0.12.0 --pyproject pyproject.toml --server-json server.json` exits 0.
- [ ] Release-specific guard and workflow tests exit 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [ ] `make test` exits 0 under the worktree virtualenv.
- [ ] `python -m build` produces the 0.12.0 wheel and sdist.
- [ ] `python -m twine check dist/*` exits 0 for the built artifacts.
- [ ] The release commit contains DCO sign-off, a Gerrit Change-Id, and this rebar-ticket trailer.
- [ ] Gerrit records LLM-Review +1 on the release change.
- [ ] Gerrit records Verified +1 on the release change.
- [ ] Gerrit has no unresolved comments on the release change.
- [ ] Gerrit submits the release change and the resulting commit is on main.
- [ ] release.yml is dispatched from main with version input 0.12.0.
- [ ] The required pypi environment deployment is approved.
- [ ] Every required release.yml job completes successfully.
- [ ] PyPI serves nava-rebar 0.12.0.
- [ ] `uvx pypi-attestations verify pypi` on the published 0.12.0 wheel with --repository https://github.com/navapbc/rebar exits 0.
- [ ] GitHub tag v0.12.0 resolves to the released main commit.
- [ ] [operator-attested] GitHub Release v0.12.0 is marked Latest.
- [ ] [operator-attested] GitHub Release v0.12.0 attaches the 0.12.0 wheel and sdist.
- [ ] MCP Registry reports io.github.navapbc/rebar version 0.12.0.
- [ ] Homebrew tap Formula/rebar.rb points to the 0.12.0 PyPI sdist URL.
- [ ] Homebrew tap Formula/rebar.rb SHA-256 equals the PyPI 0.12.0 sdist digest.
- [ ] A fresh channel install of nava-rebar[mcp]==0.12.0 passes scripts/probe_rebar.py with zero failures.
- [ ] Release receipts, any exceptions, and the rollback disposition are recorded on this ticket.
